chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Karram, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I have made it upon myself to fast until the Rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him). He said: Fast, but do not fast during travel, and do not fast on the two Eids, and do not fast on the Days of Tashriq, and do not fast on the day of doubt in the month of Ramadan.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: Travel (journey where shortening of prayer applies)
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Rising One (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: The Day of Doubt (29th or 30th of Ramadan when sighting is uncertain)

ai.seo_question: What are the exceptions to a continuous fasting vow (Nadhr) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a continuous vow (*Wajib al-Nadhr*) does not suspend the established legal exemptions (*Rukhas*) for fasting, such as travel and Eid. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific vows are subject to general Quranic dispensations, ensuring that the act of worship remains valid and not burdensome during periods of legitimate relief.
